prediction_ref.short_label: Frontier-lab governance frameworks converge on shared quantitative-harm thresholds by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
The Great American AI Act discussion draft, released Thursday June 4 by Reps. Obernolte and Trahan, is the strongest external forcing function yet for this thesis. In exchange for a three-year preemption of state frontier-development laws, the draft conditions relief on a new federal disclosure: any frontier developer above roughly $500 million in prior-year gross revenue must publish a public "frontier AI framework" describing the technical and organizational protocols it uses to evaluate and manage a model's catastrophic risks - explicitly defined as a foreseeable, material risk of mass death.

That is precisely the convergence vector the prediction names. A mandatory-disclosure template applied uniformly across the over-threshold labs pushes their separately-named, separately-structured safety frameworks toward a common, quantitative catastrophic-harm shape, and the draft even codifies the Center for AI Standards and Innovation ($100M/yr authorized FY2027-2029) to write the voluntary guidelines that would standardize the harm thresholds. Today's signal is a regulatory blueprint rather than a published lab framework, but it is the clearest movement toward a shared catastrophic-risk disclosure standard the storyline has surfaced.

reference_links.label: FedScoop - Bipartisan 'Great American AI Act' draft proposes new federal AI governance framework
Nextgov/FCW - Lawmakers propose AI framework that would preempt state laws for 3 years

bridge.narrative: The draft applies one mandatory public catastrophic-risk framework uniformly to every over-threshold developer and funds a federal body to write the standardizing guidelines. That is exactly the structural force toward a shared quantitative-harm shape this thesis names: separately-built lab frameworks now have a common template and a strong incentive to converge ahead of any vote.
bridge.remaining_gap: It is a regulatory blueprint, not yet revised lab frameworks; no over-threshold developer has actually re-published toward the common shape.

prediction_ref.short_label: AI search vendors hit federal-EU-state three-front regulatory anchor by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
The Great American AI Act draft sharpens the federal-versus-state axis this prediction tracks. Its headline provision is a three-year preemption of state laws that specifically regulate frontier-model development - taking direct aim at California's AB 2013 training-data-disclosure law and part of SB 942 watermarking - while explicitly preserving state laws of general applicability and rules governing how AI is used or deployed.

The draft thus codifies an active federal-state collision and a partial federal ceiling, the U.S. legs of the multi-front regulatory map the prediction anticipates. Reaction split immediately along the preemption line, with safety advocates calling the conversion of a state-law floor into a federal ceiling a "generational mistake." The relevance is partial: today's news is a U.S. governance development with no EU-side movement, so it densifies the federal-state fronts the prediction names without speaking to the European front.

prediction_ref.short_label: Agent-harness vendors ship gVisor+OS-sandbox+VM containment specs by Q2 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
Two fresh agentic-AI advisories give this containment thesis a strong defensive data point. CVE-2026-25879 in Langroid's SQLChatAgent earned a CVSS 9.8 rating: because the agent executes model-authored SQL that prompt injection can steer, an attacker can reach dangerous dialect-specific primitives (PostgreSQL pg_execute_server_program, MySQL FILE, MSSQL xp_cmdshell) and escalate from data theft to full remote code execution on the database host when the agent runs under an over-privileged role. The article ties this to the actively exploited LiteLLM proxy injection (CVE-2026-42208), framing both as the same text-to-SQL-to-database pattern.

The maintainer's fix is exactly the kind of execution-layer guard this prediction expects: Langroid 0.63.0 now defaults SQLChatAgent to a sqlglot-parsed SELECT-only allowlist plus a dialect-aware dangerous-pattern blocklist, and the stated lesson is that any LLM allowed to author SQL must run against a least-privilege, read-only-by-default role. That is containment moving into the harness rather than left to the deployer - a parser/allowlist analogue of the gVisor/OS-sandbox/VM isolation the prediction names. The gap to the precise prediction is that the spec here is a SQL-allowlist guard, not the named OS-level or VM isolation primitives.

prediction_ref.short_label: Chinese open-MoE cohort crosses 15 percent OpenRouter share floor by Q3 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary:
China's MiniMax launched M3, billed as the first open-weight system to combine frontier coding-agent performance, a one-million-token context window, and native multimodality, built on a new MiniMax Sparse Attention mechanism and reportedly trained on roughly 100 trillion interleaved text-image tokens. It reports 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro - ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, approaching Claude Opus 4.7 - and 83.5 on BrowseComp.

A new Chinese open-weight frontier-class coding model is exactly the supply-side momentum behind this prediction's OpenRouter-share thesis. The relevance is tempered by two caveats that bear directly on the share-floor mechanism: the scores are company-reported on MiniMax's own infrastructure, and at launch the model is reachable only via the MiniMax API and Code app, with the weights and technical report promised on Hugging Face within about ten days but not yet shipped (the newest published checkpoint there is still M2.7). Until the weights land and the model is routable, M3 strengthens the cohort narrative without yet adding measurable open-router traffic.

The prediction centers on indirect prompt injection driving data exfiltration through agents wired into privileged systems; the Langroid SQLChatAgent flaw (CVE-2026-25879) is a clean instance - an attacker who can shape the agent's input directly via a malicious prompt or indirectly by poisoning data the model later reads can coerce dangerous SQL primitives, escalating from data theft to remote code execution.
